rule: Permission failures are explained, not silenced.

structure.subject: What action was attempted (e.g., 'Can't delete this workspace').
structure.diagnosis: Why it failed — name the missing role or scope.
structure.remedy: How to obtain access — name the role that holds it.
structure.recoveryAction: Button or link to request access where the product supports it.

appearance.inContext: Prefer inline explanation at the denied affordance over a dialog.
appearance.disabledControls: If an affordance must be disabled by permission, annotate it (tooltip + aria-describedby); never silent.
appearance.navigation: A denied route renders an explanatory page with the same structure — not a 403 blank.

refusal: Silently disabling the button — user doesn't know why.
'Something went wrong' — hides the permission diagnosis.
Exposing internal role IDs (e.g., 'role-uuid-...') — use human-readable role names.
Pretending the feature doesn't exist when the user lacks access — violates product trust.
